Form. No) 2
G. 21,500 1
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S B. REGISTRY Special Branch Date 9th Oct 1931.）
Subject (in full) "Red Literature"
Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. J.W. Prince.
Sir,
Copies of books mentioned under category "A" in the attached have been obtained and perused by members of our staff who report that although the titles and authors' names might indicate that the contents are communistic, there is nothing in any of them favourable to Communism, or of such nature as would induce readers to look upon communism in a favourable light. The books deal chiefly with biographies of well known Bolsheviks such as Lenin, Trotsky, Stalin, etc. with reference to erudition, genius, and character; their position in respect of Soviet administration during the time they were in power, and their general policies in respect of Soviet principles.
Other books deal chiefly with the difference in organization between U.S.S.R. and S.S.S.R. with regard to the ruling institutions of U.S.S.R., and outline of the national organizations of the United Soviet Republic giving details of the duties of the various officials under the Government, and general administration under local committees and authorities throughout the country.
One of the books mentioned under Category "A" entitled "Pupillary Karl Marx" we have not been able to obtain as the shop where it was published has been closed, and we have not been able to procure a copy of it in any of the bookstores in the Settlement.
Officer-in-charge
To see on return.
H.R. 21/9
（签名：J.W. Prince）
C. D. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.
（签名）
25.9.31.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
报告
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 刑事与特别股登记处 特别支部 日期 1931年10月9日。）
主题（全称）“红色文献”
由首席侦探督察 J.W. Prince 撰写并呈送。

先生，
附件中“A”类项下所列书籍的副本已由我处职员获取并审阅，他们报告称，尽管书名和作者姓名可能暗示其内容具有共产主义色彩，但其中没有任何一本书对共产主义持赞成态度，或其性质足以诱导读者以赞成的眼光看待共产主义。这些书籍主要涉及著名布尔什维克人物（如列宁、托洛茨基、斯大林等）的传记，侧重于他们的学识、天才和性格；他们在掌权期间在苏维埃行政方面的地位，以及他们在苏维埃原则方面的一般政策。

其他书籍主要论述苏联（U.S.S.R.）与苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟（S.S.S.R.）[注：此处原文如此，实指同一实体或当时译名混淆] 在统治机构方面的组织差异，概述了苏维埃共和国联盟的国家组织机构，详细说明了政府下各级官员的职责，以及全国各地地方委员会和当局的一般行政管理情况。

“A”类项下提到的一本名为《小学生的马克思》（Pupillary Karl Marx）的书，我们未能获得，因为出版该书的书店已关闭，且我们在租界内的任何书店均无法购得此书副本。

主管警官
阅后归还。
H.R. 21/9
（签名：J.W. Prince）
首席侦探督察
特别支部主管警官。
（签名）
1931年9月25日。

Special Branch,
September 3,1931.

C.D.I . Prince

Mr. Givens has expressed the view that in
cases where a shop is suspected of selling communistic
literature, copies of it should be purchased and
extracts translated, care being used to preserve
the receipt of purchase. If on submission of the parts
translated the Officer i/c is of opinion that the
contents of the book constitute an offence against the
Internal Security of the State he will submit them
to the M.A. for further advice and instructions.

Will you please therefore arrange to purchase
from the incidentals copies of the literature contained
in the list at Flag "A" which you consider to be most
"Red" and deal with it in the manner above described.

Henry Robertson
C.D.I.
for O. i/c Sp. Br.

1931年9月3日。

首席侦探督察 Prince

吉文斯先生（Mr. Givens）表示认为，在怀疑某家书店出售共产主义文献的情况下，应购买其副本并翻译摘录，同时注意保留购买收据。如果在提交翻译部分后，主管警官认为该书内容构成危害国家内部安全的罪行，他将把材料提交给总办（M.A.）以寻求进一步建议和指导。

因此，请你安排从杂项经费中购买标有“A”旗号的清单中所列你认为最“红”的文献副本，并按上述方式处理。

亨利·罗伯逊（Henry Robertson）
首席侦探督察
代特别支部主管警官

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT

File No.
Special Branch S.B. XXXX
S. B. D. 2665.
Date August 29, 1931.
" 31 - 8 - 31.

Subject (in full) Red Literature.

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. J.W. Prince.

Sir,
The article entitled "The Flood of Red Literature", which appeared in the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury on August 8, 1931, under the nom de plume "Chi Cha Feng", in which the writer alleged that the Chinese Bookstores in Shanghai were flooded with "Red Literature", was subscribed by a Chinese student who did not divulge his correct name when he submitted the article for publication, and consequently the paper refused to publish any further articles by him. The publication of this article brought forth a letter by one "Chang Ming Fu", which was published in the above paper on August 12, 1931, and in which the writer contradicts Chi Cha Feng's statements, and censures the writer, and the editor of the newspaper for having published it. Please see attached letter by Chang Ming Fu.

The editor of the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury evidently knows who "Chi Cha Feng" really is as he informed us that he is a student who is attached to one of the local offices under the Nanking Government, and that he contributed to the "China Critic", though a search through our files of this paper failed to show any articles under the nom de plume "Chi Cha Feng". He further informed us that on receipt of the letter by "Chang Ming Fu", he refused to publish any further articles by "Chi Cha Feng", and when pressed for the latter's correct name he refused to divulge it. The statement regarding "Chi Cha Feng" being attached to one of the local offices of the Nanking Government is scarcely reconcileable with the fact that the Chinese Authorities are ever on the alert for Communistic and reactionary literature, whether published in the Settlement or elsewhere, and they would be among the first to take action

“ 31 - 8 - 31.

主题（全称）红色文献。

由首席侦探督察 J.W. Prince 撰写并呈送。

先生，
1931年8月8日，《上海晚邮报与信使报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）刊登了一篇题为《红色文献泛滥》的文章，作者笔名为“Chi Cha Feng”（音译：查查风/查季峰），作者在文中声称上海的中文书店充斥着“红色文献”。该文由一名中国学生投稿，他在提交文章发表时未透露真实姓名，因此报社拒绝再刊登他的任何文章。这篇文章的发表引来了名为“Chang Ming Fu”（音译：张明甫/张明福）的人的一封信，该信于1931年8月12日在上述报纸上发表，信中作者反驳了 Chi Cha Feng 的说法，并谴责作者及报社编辑刊登此文。请参阅附上的 Chang Ming Fu 的信件。

《上海晚邮报与信使报》的编辑显然知道“Chi Cha Feng”的真实身份，因为他告诉我们，此人是一名隶属于南京政府某地方机构的学生，并且曾向《中国评论周报》（China Critic）投稿，尽管查阅我们保存的该报档案并未发现署名为“Chi Cha Feng”的任何文章。他还告诉我们，收到“Chang Ming Fu”的来信后，他拒绝再刊登“Chi Cha Feng”的任何文章，当被追问后者的真实姓名时，他拒绝透露。关于“Chi Cha Feng”隶属于南京政府某地方机构的说法，与中国当局时刻警惕共产主义和反动文献（无论是在租界还是其他地方出版）这一事实难以调和，他们本应是率先采取行动

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, August 12, 1931

Cha Chi-feng Scored
By Countryman

To The Editor:
I suppose you pay Mr. Cha Chi-feng, or whoever he is, some money for writing for you, maybe five dollars each time. But I don't know why you pay him for writing lies, half truths, or just plain ignorant things. Maybe he thinks you foreigners are so ignorant that he can pawn off ignorant things on you about Chinese. When he wrote about "Flood of Red Literature in Shanghai," he has stolen ideas and even exact words from an essay by Dr. Lin Yu-tang in the "China Critic" a few months ago. Maybe Mr. Cha thinks your readers did not read that. So he now pawns it off as his own. Then he is half-backed. He says the League of Freedom and the League of Left Writers are the same. They are not. He says League of Left Writers sent an appeal to the American working class in an American magazine "The Masses". There is no "The Masses" in America and the appeal of Left Writers was international to all writers and thinkers throughout the world. Mr. Cha says there are hundreds of Communistic books on Fooshow Road, translated by the 30 members of League of Left Writers and that these also publish a number of mosquito papers and some magazines in Shanghai. Thirty of these writers can translate hundreds of books, publish many mosquito papers and magazines in Shanghai! Mr. Cha and his crowd, even with the help of detectives and policemen he calls to his help, can not do much work.
Maybe they spent too much time in dance halls and sing-song houses each night. He says if police could search trunks of students they would find them filled with new Communist literature. But if policemen could search trunks of Mr. Cha and his friends, what would they find? Maybe some dirty sex pictures of 24 positions, maybe literature on How to Get Rich Quick by writing for The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury.
Mr. Cha knows nothing about new Chinese literature. He copies what other men write and makes some money by writing for foreign imperialist papers. He knows nothing, even to write for you.
Mr. Cha could be asked questions—we say, tell us why Chinese young men and women still read Soviet social literature of foreign to China but today a foreign liver. 2174
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1931年8月12日，星期三

查季峰遭同胞驳斥
作者：同胞

致编辑：
我想你们付给查季峰先生（Mr. Cha Chi-feng），或者不管他是谁，一些稿费，也许每次五美元。但我不知道你们为什么要付钱让他写谎言、半真半假的话，或者纯粹无知的东西。也许他认为你们外国人如此无知，以至于他可以把关于中国人的无知之事兜售给你们。当他写《上海红色文献泛滥》时，他剽窃了林语堂博士几个月前在《中国评论周报》上发表的一篇文章的观点，甚至逐字抄袭。也许查先生认为你们的读者没有读过那篇文章。所以他现在把它当作自己的作品兜售。然后他又露怯了。他说自由大同盟和左翼作家联盟是一回事。它们不是。他说左翼作家联盟在美国杂志《群众》（The Masses）上向美国工人阶级发出呼吁。美国根本没有《群众》这本杂志，左翼作家的呼吁是面向全世界所有作家和思想家的国际性呼吁。查先生说福州路有数百本共产主义书籍，由左翼作家联盟的30名成员翻译，并且这些人还在上海出版许多“蚊子报”和一些杂志。这30位作家能在上海翻译数百本书，出版许多“蚊子报”和杂志！查先生和他那群人，即使加上他叫来帮忙的侦探和警察，也干不了多少活。
也许他们每晚在舞厅和妓院花太多时间了。他说如果警察搜查学生的行李箱，会发现里面装满了新的共产主义文献。但是如果警察能搜查查先生和他朋友的行李箱，他们会发现什么？也许是一些24种姿势的淫秽色情图片，也许是关于如何通过为《上海晚邮报与信使报》撰稿而快速致富的文献。
查先生对中国新文学一无所知。他抄袭别人写的东西，通过为外国帝国主义报纸撰稿来赚钱。他一无所知，甚至不配为你们撰稿。
可以向查先生提出问题——我们要说，告诉我们为什么中国青年男女仍然阅读源自外国但如今已是外来物的苏联社会文学。我们倾向于依赖我们所拥有的帽子[注：此处原文逻辑混乱，似为OCR错误或原文语病] 爱是引用的补充道：“在平等基础上的条约。”敦促和解政策，抗议使用……向国王发送了一封电报“在1927年2月发生了相当大的劳工……抗议承认其无知的行动……上海当时各种北方……例子发生在1925年，期间变得严重……

SPECIAL INQUIRY

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
C. & S. I. REC.
No. S. B. D. 2665.
Date 10 - 8 - 31）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, August 8, 1931

The Flood Of Red Literature

By CHI CHA-TING

THIRTY divisions of Government troops are engaged in the suppression of Red Army in Central China. However not a single policeman pays any attention to this matter near at hand in Shanghai.

Probably it is true as reported that all Party members and Governmental officials know the fact, but it is true to a greater extent than they have the courage to admit to themselves; there is an overwhelming tide of "Red" literature published and sold in Shanghai.

Anybody who visits the book shops on Foochow Road will see that practically all books in stock of these book shops have something to do with Soviet Russia, Karl Marx, Lenin, Stalin and a number of others with their names ending with a lev or an ov.

The works of Russian authors translated into Chinese in the last two years which one can find in these bookshops serve as a collection of Soviet Literature which would put many a library in Europe or America to shame.

Among the many authors of these books, one find these names: Lebediensky, Fedeev, Kollontay, Yakovlev, Pilniak, Ahnyov, Iva, Lhuts, Demidov, Ivanov, Shaginian, Sosnovsky, Fedin, Vessely, Volkov, Sobole, Lidin, Figner, NVNV, Rabel, Arosev, Gladkov, Neverov, Formanov, and a number of others. All these books are translated into Chinese. A number of them have two or three simultaneous translations. Gladkov's Cement has three translations. Ognyov's Diary of a Communist Schoolboy has three translations. Kollontay's Red Love has two. All these show the feverish demand for things Russian.

The popularity of "Red Litera-

ture" tells one thing. That is the conquering of Young China by Russia. If one takes the trouble to search the trunks of school and college students, large numbers of these books would be found. The interest of young Chinese on matters Communistic is a sign of great significance. The destiny of China in the next thirty years hangs upon them!

Already there is the "Liberty League" or rather "Left Writers' League" as another report puts it, in Shanghai. This League has about thirty writers as its members with the famous writer Lu-hsin as their leader. They even appealed to the masses of America for support in an open letter to the American workers as published in the American magazine The Masses.

Writers of this League are busily engaged themselves in the translation of Russian books and the publication of a number of Chinese magazines. It is understood that a number of "mosquito papers" have their origin from the pens of these people.

The general Communistic movement in China can not be fully understood without paying attention to this fact. In the early part of 1920, the beginning of Communistic teachings in this country, we had the famous writers, such as: Chen Tu-hsu and Li Tai-chao, both of whom were professors of the former Peking University.

It was through the writings of these people that large numbers of young Chinese turned their attention to the Communistic teachings and brought about the organization of Red Army and Soviet Governments in Central China. The suppression of Red Army will not solve the entire problem. These young faithful visitors of Foochow Road bookshops will become a real problem in the coming future.

A definite policy on the part of the National Government is necessary to cope with the situation. It is the duty of the authorities to see what kind of citizens they want to turn out in the next generation.

（批：6. S. I. Prince,
For investigation and
report please.
WC

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1931年8月8日，星期六

红色文学的泛滥

作者：季扎廷 (CHI CHA-TING)

政府军三十个师正致力于围剿华中地区的红军。然而，在上海这一近在咫尺的地方，竟无一名警察对此事予以关注。

据报道，所有党员和政府官员均知晓这一事实，这或许属实；但实际情况比他们敢于向自己承认的程度更为严重：上海出版和销售的“红色”文学正呈汹涌之势。

任何走访福州路书店的人都会发现，这些书店库存中的书籍几乎都与苏维埃俄国、卡尔·马克思、列宁、斯大林以及其他许多名字以“列夫”或“奥夫”结尾的人物有关。

在这些书店中可以找到的、过去两年内翻译成中文的俄罗斯作家作品，其数量之丰足以构成一套苏维埃文学丛书，令欧美许多图书馆相形见绌。

在这些书籍的众多作者中，可以看到以下名字：列别甸斯基 (Lebediensky)、法捷耶夫 (Fedeev)、柯伦泰 (Kollontay)、雅科夫列夫 (Yakovlev)、皮利尼亚克 (Pilniak)、阿尼约夫 (Ahnyov)、伊瓦 (Iva)、卢茨 (Lhuts)、杰米多夫 (Demidov)、伊万诺夫 (Ivanov)、沙吉尼扬 (Shaginian)、索斯诺夫斯基 (Sosnovsky)、费丁 (Fedin)、韦谢雷 (Vessely)、沃尔科夫 (Volkov)、索博列 (Sobole)、利金 (Lidin)、菲格纳 (Figner)、NVNV、拉贝尔 (Rabel)、阿罗谢夫 (Arosev)、格拉德科夫 (Gladkov)、涅韦罗夫 (Neverov)、福尔马诺夫 (Formanov) 以及许多其他人。所有这些书籍均已译成中文。其中不少作品同时存在两到三种译本。格拉德科夫的《水泥》有三种译本。奥格尼奥夫的《一个共产主义少先队员的日记》有三种译本。柯伦泰的《红色爱情》有两种译本。所有这些都表明了对俄罗斯事物的狂热需求。

“红色文

学”的流行说明了一个问题。那就是俄罗斯对年轻中国的征服。如果有人费心去搜查中小学生的行李箱，就会发现大量此类书籍。中国青年对共产主义事务的兴趣是一个具有重大意义的迹象。中国未来三十年的命运取决于他们！

上海已经出现了“自由同盟”，或者如另一份报告所称，“左翼作家联盟”。该联盟约有三十名作家成员，由著名作家鲁迅担任领袖。他们甚至在美国杂志《群众》(The Masses) 上发表了一封致美国工人的公开信，呼吁美国民众给予支持。

该联盟的作家们正忙于翻译俄罗斯书籍并出版多种中文杂志。据悉，许多“蚊子报”均出自这些人之手。

如果不关注这一事实，就无法充分理解中国的共产主义运动。在1920年代初期，即共产主义学说在本国传播之初，我们有诸如陈独秀和李大钊等著名作家，两人均为前北京大学的教授。

正是通过这些人的著作，大批中国青年将注意力转向了共产主义学说，从而促成了华中地区红军和苏维埃政府的组织。围剿红军并不能解决整个问题。这些福州路书店的年轻忠实顾客将在未来成为真正的问题。

国民政府需要制定明确的政策来应对这一局势。当局有责任审视他们希望下一代培养出什么样的公民。

（批注：6. S. I. Prince，
请调查并
提交报告。
WC
1931年8月10日。）
